findings.issue: History-axis dates are reconstructed from positive-gross box-office rows. A degraded production refresh with no resolved grosses leaves no durable record, so a later forecast build omits that refresh and connects the line across the missing observation, contrary to §5.6 and §12.4.
findings.suggestion: Persist every production refresh date independently of gross and forecast rows, then use those dates to construct the history axis.

findings.issue: After a candidate title is canonicalized through `alias_of`, override metadata is looked up only under the canonical title. If the variant's override entry also supplies `category`, `release_date`, or `status`—all allowed together by §5.4—those corrections are discarded, potentially selecting the wrong projection model or date.
findings.suggestion: Canonicalize and merge override metadata before building films, preserving metadata attached to alias entries and rejecting conflicting corrections explicitly.

findings.issue: `matrix_rows` is accepted as any positive integer, including values below 10. Such a configuration makes the leaderboard and What If page construct their scoring finish order from fewer than ten films even while the simulation scores a full top ten, producing inconsistent totals and omitting the mandatory top-ten cutoff.
findings.suggestion: Require `matrix_rows >= 10` at the Season load boundary.

findings.issue: Pre-opening entries are constructed without validating field types. Quoted numeric estimates or a non-date `release_date` load successfully and then fail later in `is_complete`, date comparison, or projection arithmetic, violating §5's requirement that bad persisted data fail at the load boundary.
findings.suggestion: Validate date fields, numeric estimate fields, and textual fields before constructing `PreopeningEstimate`, raising a path-and-title-specific ValueError.

findings.issue: `group_id` is returned without verifying that it is a directory-safe slug. Values such as `../other` are accepted despite §3.3 requiring a stable slug safe for use as a directory name.
findings.suggestion: Validate `group_id` against a conservative slug rule and reject path separators, traversal components, empty values, and non-string values at load time.
